title: Day 13 · Foundation: F = ma in practice
c1: Choose the object and add its forces
q1: Point to the force missing from the crossed-out calculation on comic page 49. What net force acts on the box? Include direction.
q2: A 4 kg box accelerates right at 2 m/s². Friction is 6 N left. Find the pull. Show how it gives the net force you need.
q3: Use card C on comic page 50. Find the mass. Show your equation and unit.
q4: On page 51 the car is moving forward. Use its change in velocity to find the net force. Explain what its sign means.
q5: On your own: a 4 kg cart is pushed right with 18 N. Friction pulls left with 6 N. Find the net force and acceleration. Include direction.
a1: Friction is the missing 6 N to the left. The sum is 30 − 6 = 24 N right.
a2: The box needs 8 N net to the right. The pull is 14 N right because 14 − 6 = 8.
a3: Mass is net force divided by acceleration. Here 18 ÷ 3 gives 6 kg.
a4: Acceleration is (0 − 30) ÷ 5 = −6 m/s². The net force is −9,000 N, opposite the car’s forward motion.
a5: The net force is 12 N right. Dividing by 4 kg gives 3 m/s² right.
ex1: A student says the box feels 30 N right, so 30 N must be the net force.
ex2: A student says a pull of 8 N is enough when the net force must be 8 N and friction is 6 N left.
ex3: A student says a car with a negative net force must already be moving backward.
